panels.description: Wide, full page width. The Travancore coast under a hard midday sun, glare off a flat sea. A finger of sandy headland pushing out into the water, coconut palms leaning inland. On the far horizon, very small, a row of white specks.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Late in 1739, the horizon changed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not yet the war fleet that would come two years later. Only a probing squadron, sent to count our guns. We did not know that then.

panels.description: Low angle straight up the trunk of one tall palm. At its crown, a rough wooden platform lashed on with rope. A lanky boy of about fifteen stands on it, all elbows and shins, threadbare cloth whipping in the sea wind, a long brass spyglass to his eye.

copy.speaker: BOY (from above)
copy.text: Three ships. No, four. The new one is smaller.

panels.description: Ground level at the foot of the palm. A Nair guard with a spear craning his neck upward. Behind him, coming up the sandy path, Nagoji and Ibrahim on horseback.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: The banded flag?

copy.speaker: BOY (from above)
copy.text: Red, white, blue.

panels.description: The guard turns to Nagoji, squinting against the light.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: Company ships. Dutch.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He said it in Hindustani, for the foreigner.

panels.description: Nagoji's point of view, out to sea. Four hulls on the horizon line, still small and distant: three large East Indiamen and one smaller square-rigged consort, sails full, moving in slow procession along the line where sky meets water.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We had marched north and swallowed Kollam. In swallowing the small fish, we had drawn the eye of the shark.

panels.description: The boy grinning down from his platform, glass lowered, one arm hooked around the palm.

copy.speaker: BOY
copy.text: They are closer than yesterday.

copy.speaker: BOY
copy.text: These ones move like men who know where they are going.

panels.description: Nagoji looking up, one hand shading his eyes (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And who leads them?

copy.speaker: BOY (from above)
copy.text: The same tall captain. The one with the pale hair and the stick he uses to beat his men into straight lines.

panels.description: The boy's view through the spyglass, a soft-edged circular vignette. Far off, the high stern of the largest ship, and on it a tiny, stiff, dark silhouette of a tall man, hands clasped behind his back, the outline of a black tricorne, a dark blue tone to the coat. Only a pale glint at the collar where his hair shows. No features, no readable detail.

copy.speaker: GUARD (off)
copy.text: He drills them until they piss in step.

copy.speaker: BOY (off)
copy.text: When he turns, the men move. When he scratches his nose, they move slower.

panels.description: Nagoji turning his horse, calling up to the boy. The boy already has the glass back at his eye.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Keep watching. Count how many days they hover. Count how close they dare come.

panels.description: Riding back down the sandy path, Nagoji and Ibrahim side by side, the palm lookout small behind them against the sea.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: They smell blood. Or pepper. To them it is the same.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They smell a king who does not kneel easily.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: That too.

panels.description: Wide. The war hall in afternoon heat. Maps unrolled across the floor, held flat by stones and spear shafts, scattered with pebbles and shells as tokens. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) crouched over one map. Marthanda Varma (V13 varma-v1 face) sits cross-legged on the floor itself, bare-chested and glistening with heat, his hair pulled back under a narrow white cloth band (not a turban), his spear laid aside. Nagoji in the doorway, backlit (commander sheet, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin), with Ibrahim a step behind him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The war hall smelled of ink and sweat.

copy.speaker: VARMA (not looking up)
copy.text: Sawant. Tell me.

panels.description: Nagoji kneeling at the edge of the map (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Four company ships. Three large, one smaller. Moving south.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The same tall officer on the quarterdeck. Pale hair, stiff back. He drills them hard.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Ramayyan's thin fingers setting a small white shell beside a charcoal smear that marks a headland.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Here. If they hold that course and that speed.

panels.description: Ibrahim stepping forward into the light, nodding at the shell.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: They will anchor within sight of our coast by evening. Close enough to send boats ashore.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Gifts for those who fear you more than the company. Promises written in thick ink and broken in thin whispers.

panels.description: Varma looking up for the first time, straight at Nagoji.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They test us. They want to see how high we raise our hackles when they show their teeth.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: What would your Peshwa do?

panels.description: Nagoji speaking (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin). Behind him, ghosted into the war hall like a watermark, Pune's court: painted pillars, a high seat, scribes and sardars.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He would send letters. But he would not move his own men until he had counted the cost twice.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: His coast is not as tightly bound to his capital as yours is. He can afford to pretend distance.

panels.description: Varma, flat and certain.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I cannot. If the Dutch piss in our waters, the smell reaches my throne the same day.

panels.description: Ramayyan's stylus scratching a palm leaf. He does not lift his eyes.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: These ships answer to the Zeeland chamber of the company.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Their commander is cautioned not to provoke open war. Only to remind local chiefs who controls trade. He will test alliances.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: And our sand drills? What do they make of those?

panels.description: Tight on Varma's finger tapping the map, once, beside the white shell.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: I want them to glimpse enough to worry.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: Not enough to understand.

panels.description: Close on Varma, looking at Nagoji. Something in his face has shifted: an account being acknowledged.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I have not forgotten what you did in February.

panels.description: Large, top half. An open beach pavilion at Tengapattanam, night, half past eleven. The king's procession approaching under umbrellas, lit by torches; Malabar women at the roadside with hands raised to their mouths, ululating, their faces caught in firelight. Opposite, Dutch trumpeters and drummers in VOC blue coats answering, and behind them ranks of Dutch soldiers drawn up in lines, torchlight on their musket barrels.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: February. Eight months before.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Van Imhoff, the Dutch Governor of Ceylon, came with three hundred men, gifts worth thousands, and a list of demands.

panels.description: Ramayyan leaning in to whisper in the king's ear. Varma in his court look: V13 varma-v1 face, cream and gold, peacock crest, gold necklaces, bare-chested. Behind them, out of focus, Nagoji (rust-red turban) and Dhanaji (white pagdi, short black beard).

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (whisper)
copy.text: Let Van Imhoff wonder whether the Peshwa's men ride south for pepper or for alliance.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (whisper)
copy.text: A question he cannot answer is worth more than a hundred soldiers he can count.

panels.description: Nagoji standing behind the king's seat in lamplight, talwar on show, scarred hands and ridged nails visible, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin. Dhanaji on his right; beyond them the four riders in off-white turbans. A hard, still line.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We were placed as if we were merely guards.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We were not guards. We were theatre.

panels.description: Van Imhoff in the left foreground, three-quarter back view: a heavy-set Dutch governor in his thirties, dark coat with gold braid, a full powdered wig, his head turned to look past the king. Across the pavilion, behind the king's seat, Nagoji in the rust-red turban stands at the king's shoulder, head turned toward the bearded Dhanaji on his right, muttering something sideways.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had no way of knowing I was a fugitive. No letter from Pune, no Peshwa's blessing, no army behind me.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He saw what we wanted him to see. A southern king with Deccan steel at his back.

panels.description: Van Imhoff and Varma across a low table, interpreters kneeling between them, lamps on the table. Civil. Careful. Every man counting.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He wanted pepper contracts, and trading posts at Colachel and Vizhinjam. The king wanted help against Chanda Sahib.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Neither man gave ground.

panels.description: Varma, smiling, perfectly calm.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: One thousand kalanjus. For the hiranyagarbha ceremony.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: A gesture of friendship from the Company.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji behind the king's seat, lamplight on his face (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin), watching Van Imhoff.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The rite that would make him twice-born, and entitle him to be crowned Kulasekhara Perumal, sovereign of all Kerala.

panels.description: Tight on Van Imhoff's mouth, smiling.

copy.speaker: VAN IMHOFF
copy.text: Eight.

panels.description: Medium three-shot. Varma fills the centre, still smiling, but his jaw has set. In the lower foreground, Ramayyan's hand, the stylus stopped above his leaf. Above Varma's shoulder, Nagoji's eyes, narrowed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Less than one percent. Not a negotiation. A message: the Company did not want him crowned.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They measured out their contempt in gold and called it diplomacy.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It would be answered.

panels.description: The war hall, present day. Varma leaning over the map now, one finger tracing the coastline.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Now, eight months later, the answer was taking shape.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Take a small party of riders along the coast. In sight of their ships, out of cannon range.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Let their glass see horse that do not fear the water's edge.

panels.description: Nagoji, a dry half smile (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They will think we mean to charge the sea.

panels.description: Varma.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Let them think many things. Confusion is a useful ally.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We will not fire first. But we will not lower our heads either.

panels.description: Ramayyan setting pebbles along the map's creeks, its market towns, a temple mark.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Our men on the backwaters will count their boats. Our scribes in the markets will listen.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Our temple men will note which sleeves carry new gold.

panels.description: Overhead, the whole map. From the single white shell, tokens now spread outward across the coast in widening rings, like ripples from a stone.

Large, top half. A long hall open on one side to the sea breeze, wooden pillars, mats across the floor, lamps lit against the shaded interior, a hanging cloth at the open side lifting in the breeze. Marthanda Varma on a low platform, not a throne. Men and women seated in clusters rather than ranks. Padmini Amma (fifties, thick black hair coiled at the nape, simple gold, cotton sari, long walking stick) near the front. Farther back, among the older women of Velinadu, Revathi Bayi in a deep green sari (a widow: no tali, no sindoor in the parting; the sandalwood line at her hairline is her only forehead mark). Nagoji against a pillar at the side (commander sheet, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Three days later, the Dutch came to court. Not the men from the ships. Men with account books and careful smiles.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Court here did not look like court in Pune.

panels.description: Ramayyan at the king's right, leaf bundles stacked neatly, stylus loose in his hand, eyes moving. On the king's left, an empty cleared space on the mats. Nagoji's shoulder in the foreground edge.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That space was for the Dutch.

panels.description: The Dutch entering. Two envoys, drawn so they cannot be confused. The LEAD ENVOY, the older of the two: heavy, in his fifties, hair streaked grey at the temples and tied back in a black ribbon queue, no wig, a very dark brown coat cut tight at the waist with rows of brass buttons, lace at the cuffs, no gold braid, a black tricorne under his arm. The SECOND ENVOY, a step behind: thinner, brown hair tied back, a charcoal-grey coat, a black tricorne under his arm. Neither coat is VOC blue. Behind them, younger clerks carrying account books, and an interpreter of mixed Portuguese and Indian features whose eyes slide everywhere and settle nowhere.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They came with the heavy formality of men told to be polite to people they considered their inferiors.

panels.description: Varma in his court look: V13 varma-v1 face, cream and gold, peacock crest, gold necklaces, bare-chested, with a simple cloth over one shoulder and a string of rudraksha beads among the gold; no crown. In the foreground the lead envoy (heavy, dark brown coat, grey-streaked queue) bowing slightly, the interpreter at his elbow.

copy.speaker: ENVOY
copy.text: Maharaja. The Honourable Company brings greetings, and hopes for continued friendship.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You bring ships that sit like crows on our water. Is that how your company shows friendship?

panels.description: The interpreter caught out, blinking before he translates. Beside him the lead envoy (dark brown coat, grey-streaked queue), his mouth tightening very slightly.

copy.speaker: ENVOY
copy.text: Our ships patrol the coast to protect trade. There are pirates.

copy.speaker: ENVOY
copy.text: The seas are not as peaceful as we would like.

panels.description: Varma, unhurried.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Nor is the land.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Yet you do not see my horse standing in your streets in Batavia.

panels.description: Wide. A ripple through the hall: local chiefs smiling behind their hands. At the front, Padmini Amma, stick across her knees, the barest amusement in her eyes.
Split panel: two thin, tight strips side by side. Left strip, Varma's eyes. Right strip, Padmini's eyes. Their eyelines meet across the gutter. One heartbeat, unguarded.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Then it vanished back into politics.

panels.description: Farther back, among the Velinadu women: Revathi Bayi. Deep green sari, jewellery quieter than before, jasmine in her braid, sandalwood line at her hairline, the flat-coin necklace; no tali, no sindoor in the parting. She is looking at the envoy.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi Bayi. Less gold than at our first meeting.

panels.description: The lead envoy (dark brown coat, grey-streaked queue) spreading his hands, his eyes flicking toward the Velinadu women and then to Padmini.

copy.speaker: ENVOY
copy.text: We wish only to reaffirm our treaties with the important houses of this coast.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He knew enough to know where land lay.

panels.description: Revathi speaking, chin lifted. Heads across the hall turning toward her as if someone had moved a lamp.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She answered in Portuguese. She needed no interpreter.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Our treaties stand. They say nothing of the company telling my kin in Travancore how many muskets to buy, or whom to marry.

panels.description: The lead envoy, faintly surprised, inclining his head more deeply than he did for any chief.

copy.speaker: ENVOY
copy.text: Princess. We know the history of your line. We come with renewed respect.

panels.description: Reverse shot from behind Revathi's shoulder: her braid with jasmine and the edge of her green sari in the near foreground. Across the hall, small in the middle ground, the lead envoy, and behind him a young Dutch clerk shifting on his feet.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Respect is shown in actions, not words.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Last time your company men came to Velinadu with arrogance, many of them fed the earth. We have not forgotten. I doubt their widows have either.

panels.description: Close on Revathi. The envoy's balloon tails in from off panel.

copy.speaker: ENVOY (off)
copy.text: Those events belonged to another time. Another management.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Our memories do not change when your clerk's handwriting does.

panels.description: Varma lifting one hand, ending the exchange.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We are not here to relive old mistakes. We are here to see whether new ones can be avoided.

panels.description: Wide on a cluster of three local chiefs, their designs locked for this chapter. The HAIR-STICK CHIEF: wiry, middle-aged, hair tied up with a carved wooden stick, a thin shoulder cloth. The GOLD-CHAIN CHIEF: fleshy, draped in layers of heavy gold chains, rings on his fingers. The CHIEF IN WHITE: lean and upright, a clean white mundu and shoulder cloth, no ornaments at all, hands still on his knees.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The gold chains looked more like debt than wealth.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: You owe tax to my throne, promises to Velinadu and oaths to the Dutch. That is a great many directions for your heads to bow.

panels.description: The hair-stick chief, choosing boldness over the nervous laughter around him.

copy.speaker: CHIEF WITH HAIR STICK
copy.text: We are pulled like rope in a tug of war. We wish only that the rope not break.

panels.description: Ramayyan, soft, his eyes resting not on the chief he answers but somewhere past him, his stylus moving on the leaf. Small inset in the lower right corner, wordless: the gold-chain chief's eyes flicking once over his shoulder toward the back of the hall, where Ibrahim (short, broad, scar from the LEFT ear to the jaw) stands small against a rear pillar.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Rope breaks when it is worn or rotten.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Would you rather be tied to a king who lives among you, or to a company whose masters sit beyond the sea?

panels.description: The gold-chain chief in the foreground, speaking, his chains catching the lamplight. Behind him, soft focus toward the front of the hall, Padmini Amma, not turning her head.

copy.speaker: CHIEF IN GOLD CHAINS
copy.text: The company pays fair weight. Twelve varahans the candi, in good gold pagodas.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Fair weight. And then they sell that pepper at three times the price elsewhere. Ask them what is fair.

panels.description: The chief in white (lean, upright, no ornaments), shifting slightly, speaking quietly.

copy.speaker: CHIEF IN WHITE
copy.text: What of Kottarakkara?

copy.speaker: CHIEF IN WHITE
copy.text: The Elayadathu chief still receives Dutch factors. His sister's daughter writes to Velinadu. There are whispers.

panels.description: A strip of four small insets inside one panel, the same instant: Varma's jaw tightening. Ramayyan's stylus stopped mid-stroke. Padmini's knuckles pale around her stick. Revathi utterly still, her face a mask.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The name dropped into the hall like a stone into still water.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I watched the ripples.

panels.description: Wide, silent. The whole hall frozen, the lamp flames standing straight.
Varma, his voice carefully even.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Kottarakkara will be addressed in its time.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We are not here to discuss houses that have not yet learned to count.

panels.description: The chief in white lowering his eyes. Beyond him, Nagoji at his pillar (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin), looking not at the chief but at Revathi.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had asked a question he already knew the answer to. He wanted to see who flinched.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Something lived in those syllables that I did not yet understand.

panels.description: Wide, from behind Varma's low platform: his bare shoulders and peacock crest in the foreground, the whole audience spread out before him. The three chiefs in their cluster, the Velinadu women with Revathi in green, Padmini near the front, the Dutch party in the cleared space to his left, Nagoji at his pillar at the side.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: This land is not theirs. The roads are not theirs. The fields are not theirs.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The men who die when guns fire are not theirs.

panels.description: Tight on a young Dutch clerk's hands: an open account book on his knees, his quill stopped above the page, the terms landing. The page shows only illegible marks. Varma's balloons tail in from off panel.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: You will have your pepper. You will pay for it. You will build no new forts on this coast without my consent.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: You will not arm my enemies.

panels.description: Over Varma's shoulder (bare shoulder and gold necklaces soft in the foreground) onto the lead envoy's face, very still.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: In return, your ships will be supplied, and your merchants safe from bandits who think Europeans make sound targets.

copy.speaker: ENVOY
copy.text: And if we refuse?

panels.description: Over Nagoji's shoulder at his pillar: the edge of his rust-red turban and his shoulder in the near foreground. Across the hall, Ramayyan beside the king, his eyes turned straight toward Nagoji, and toward us. At the open side of the hall, a hanging cloth hangs dead slack, not a fold stirring.
Close on Varma, low and even.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Then you test our patience.

panels.description: Tighter. His eyes.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: And our sand.

panels.description: A memory flicker with soft edges: horses churning through wet sand, matchlock smoke drifting over surf, and high on his palm the boy with the glass.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The words were simple. The weight behind them was not.

panels.description: The lead envoy (dark brown coat, grey-streaked queue). His jaw shifts; a calculation moves behind his eyes.

copy.speaker: ENVOY
copy.text: We will convey your words to our superiors. Meanwhile, a written agreement, signed by you, the Velinadu house, and the leading landholders.

panels.description: Split tier, two narrow panels side by side. Left: Revathi, far back among the Velinadu women, lifting her chin. Right: Ramayyan at the king's right, stylus already moving.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: We will read every line. Twice.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: And we will draft some of our own. Our scribes are not as slow as you may think.

panels.description: Wide. The hall in slanting afternoon light, talk in clusters, the interpreter moving between groups, Ramayyan steering it all with small movements of one hand.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The rest of the afternoon passed in Portuguese, Malayalam and Tamil. Mutual defence. Exclusive rights. Tariffs.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I listened, and I watched.

panels.description: A strip of three small insets: Padmini's fingers tapping her stick. Revathi's nostrils flaring. A young Dutch clerk whispering into the lead envoy's ear.
During a break, Revathi has drifted along the edge of the crowd until she stands beside Nagoji at his pillar. She does not look at him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She spoke Konkani. Few in that hall could follow.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You have been very quiet, Sawant. Does all this talk bore a man who prefers the noise of hooves?

panels.description: Nagoji, his eyes still on the room (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: On the contrary. I am learning how many ways there are to start wars without lifting a sword.

panels.description: Revathi, a short pleased hum, the corner of her mouth moving.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Good. If you are to serve here, you must learn to hear when a word carries the weight of a musket.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Otherwise you will charge at the wrong time.

panels.description: Revathi tilting her head toward a chief across the hall, seated in a different cluster from the three chiefs of 12.2. He must not resemble the chief in white: older and heavier, grey-streaked hair in a side knot, a bright red-bordered shoulder cloth, a brass betel box at his knee, mouth open mid-speech, one arm flung wide as he talks loudly to his neighbours.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Two years ago he took Dutch coin to rebuild his flooded fields. Payable in pepper at harvest.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Today he speaks loudly about loyalty. When they come to collect, I wonder whose banner he will stand under.

panels.description: Nagoji turning to look at her properly (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And you? Under whose banner will you stand, when the king and the company pull in different directions?

panels.description: Revathi, looking at him as if he had asked whether the sea preferred high or low tide.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I stand under Velinadu's.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: The others move around us and hope we do not notice when they step on our toes.

panels.description: Low evening light. The Dutch party bowing out of the hall, the two envoys with their tricornes in hand. The interpreter, last in line, glances back over his shoulder at Nagoji, quick and curious.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: To him I was a foreigner in this hall, yet not European. A piece on the board whose shape he had not yet accounted for.

panels.description: Nagoji at his pillar, the faintest smile under the thick moustache, clean-shaven chin, watching them go.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Good.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Let them wonder.

panels.description: A small limewashed room open on one side to a narrow courtyard. Ramayyan leading Nagoji in (commander sheet, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin). A single man on a low stool, a clay cup of water untouched at his feet: Karl August, pale with a sickly yellow cast, cropped greying hair, bareheaded, no coat and no uniform, only a rough cotton shirt and dhoti hanging awkwardly on a frame that still remembers a uniform.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: This is Karl August. He once wore the company's blue coat.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Now he wears ours, when he wears anything at all.

panels.description: Karl August rising, stiff with old pains, inclining his head.

copy.speaker: KARL AUGUST
copy.text: I fought for the Dutch. They did not pay. They did not feed. They left us to rot in mud and fever.

copy.speaker: KARL AUGUST
copy.text: I decided I preferred to rot on my own terms.

panels.description: Insert, tight on a fresh palm leaf spread on the floor. Karl August's charcoal drawing a curve of coast, then a small square with one corner shaded. No written labels on the leaf.

copy.speaker: KARL AUGUST (off)
copy.text: Colachel. Mud fort, half fallen. Powder and rice, too close together.

copy.speaker: KARL AUGUST (off)
copy.text: They keep them in their little church. Stone keeps damp out better than canvas.

panels.description: Karl August kneeling, charcoal making a second mark offshore, his yellowed face lifted to Nagoji.

copy.speaker: KARL AUGUST
copy.text: Kanyakumari camp. Men sick. Smallpox. No pay.

copy.speaker: KARL AUGUST
copy.text: They hate their officers more than you do.

panels.description: Ramayyan looking down at the leaf with the calm of a man fitting a piece into a puzzle he almost understood already.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: We will not win this war with bravery alone.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: We will win it with men who know where the enemy keeps his fire and his food.

panels.description: Wide. A copper sky. Nagoji and Ibrahim on horseback along a ridge above the beach, silhouettes deliberately against the light; Nagoji's rust-red turban, thick moustache and clean-shaven chin edge-lit in profile. Offshore, far closer inshore than on page 1 (three days on), the Dutch East Indiamen sit dark against pale water, whole hulls and gunport strakes visible a few miles out.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That evening I rode the ridge, where their glass could find me.

panels.description: Nagoji's view through Ibrahim's spyglass, circular vignette. A hull's flank with its painted gunport strake, the gunports open, shut, open. Tiny figures on deck adjusting ropes.

Through the glass, closer: on the quarterdeck of the largest ship, a tall man in a Dutch blue coat. Hands clasped behind his back, feet planted apart against the roll, a black tricorne shading his face, pale hair escaping at the collar. Distant. No clear features.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The boy had not exaggerated. I had seen that stillness in Deccan officers who lived for drill and order.

panels.description: Nagoji lowering the glass, then half raising it again (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin). Ibrahim beside him, reins loose.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: He is just a man. He will bleed like any other if you cut him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Until I see him on land, it is hard not to think of him as part of the ship.

panels.description: Ibrahim, dry, not looking at him.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Then imagine him drowning. That will help.

panels.description: Wide, looking down from the ridge. A handful of Maravar riders trotting their horses through the shallows, water splashing to the horses' knees. Farther inland, carts creak along a track at a deliberately slow pace.
Reverse angle, far out on the water. Along the rail of the largest ship, tiny glass lenses glint in the last light, turned toward the shore.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (off)
copy.text: The tall one will note that your riders do not panic when the waves reach their hooves.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (off)
copy.text: Somewhere, a man with a powdered wig will tap that line and frown.

panels.description: Nagoji handing the glass back to Ibrahim.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Good. Let his wig itch.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: I should ride ahead. There are men in Kollam with contracts on both sides.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Both sides?

panels.description: Ibrahim facing us, the scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw clear in the low light, his eyes meeting Nagoji's. The easy merchant's charm has dropped away; under it, a calculation as cold as Ramayyan's.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: I sell to whoever keeps this coast free enough for men like me to keep selling.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Today, that is your king.

panels.description: Ibrahim already kicking his horse into motion along the ridge, one hand spread over his shoulder. Nagoji left behind against the copper sea.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Tomorrow? The sea does not care about flags. Neither do I.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: An oath of loyalty, or a warning. I could not tell which.

panels.description: Dusk in the emptying hall, the last chiefs drifting out. Ramayyan adding final lines to his leaves by lamplight, Nagoji seated on the mat beside him (commander sheet, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin).

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Dutch left angry. They know the King is shifting the pepper trade to the Syrian Christians. Tharakan and his kin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And the other chiefs?

panels.description: Ramayyan, not looking up from the leaf.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They grumble. Houses like Elayadathu prefer the Portuguese or the Dutch. They think white skin means heavier gold.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Why not his own kind? Are there no Hindu merchants?

panels.description: Ramayyan's dry, thin smile.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You are from the Deccan, Sawant. For a Hindu of good caste to cross the black water is to lose his caste.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The ocean is kalapani.

panels.description: Tight on Ramayyan's hand, closing over a few peppercorns on the mat.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: We can farm the pepper. We can tax the pepper. We cannot sail with it. That sin we leave to others.

panels.description: Nagoji and Ramayyan in the last of the lamplight, Ramayyan holding another leaf, its edge dark with handling.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And the English at Anchuthengu?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: A Company doctor there lent us coin against Chanda Sahib. They call it a loan. We call it buying time.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You trust him?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I trust his fear.

panels.description: Wide, night. The bluff above the sea, an older watchman pacing far in the background. Nagoji sits at the rock edge, knees drawn up, arms resting on them (commander sheet, rust-red turban, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin). Out on the black water, only clusters of lights; the masts are invisible.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Somewhere on the largest hull, the pale-haired officer stood or slept or paced. I did not yet know his name.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That would come later, when he surrendered at Colachel and chose a different flag.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's face (thick moustache, clean-shaven chin), the ship lights in his eyes. Ghosted behind him, bleeding in from the panel edge like a stain: a vaulted stone wall, a brazier's glow, the edge of a plain wooden table with tools laid out. No ropes, no noose, no figures.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In Goa, my enemies had been men I could smell across a torture room.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Here they hovered beyond sight, their decisions sealed with wax hundreds of leagues away.

panels.description: Nagoji's palm pressed flat against the rough rock beside him. Ridged nails, the edge of the brand on the inner left forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, just visible.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (quiet)
copy.text: Come closer. Come stand where I can reach you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (quiet)
copy.text: Let us see how your neat lines fare when the ground shifts under you.

panels.description: The lights offshore, and a faint haze smudging one cluster of them. In the near foreground, Nagoji's head turned toward it, nostrils flared, eyes narrowed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The sea gave no answer. It rarely does.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not coconut husk. Not jackfruit wood.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: Ship smoke. Dutch smoke.

panels.description: Full width, pulling far back. The tiny figure on the bluff, the long dark coast, and four clusters of light on the sea.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The horizon had begun to move nearer, whether it wished to or not.
